findings.title: Findings converge on the watcher's reconcile pipeline serving a synchronous manual caller
findings.why_it_matters: D7 routes the manual reload-all through the watcher's pipeline (`handle_change_event` → `apply_changes` → `_restart_apps_unlocked`). That pipeline was built for a caller that never waits for an answer. It returns `None`, logs per-app outcomes instead of returning them, and before bootstrap release it records a deferred reconciliation and returns without a word. On an invalid `hassette.toml` it logs the error and keeps the old config instead of raising. It also suspends between taking `_change_event_lock` and taking the key locks. Five findings each patch one of these properties: where eviction sits inside the batch restart (4), a second orchestrator that the Summary and D7 describe differently (7), returning outcomes (8), the pre-release answer (9), and an atomic busy check (10). D7's own invalid-config refusal needs a signal `refresh_config` doesn't give either (verified during synthesis, not raised by a critic). Does this mean how a synchronous caller enters the pipeline should be decided once, rather than patched five times? That re-evaluation is open-ended. It includes whether the manual path should share the watcher's pipeline at all.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate how a synchronous caller enters the reconcile pipeline before addressing Findings 4, 7, 8, 9 and 10 individually. Open questions: one entry point for watcher and manual triggers, or two? Where does eviction sit relative to the stops? How do outcomes, an invalid-config refusal and a pre-release refusal get back to the caller? Where does the busy check sit relative to the awaits in `refresh_config`?
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate how a synchronous caller enters the reconcile pipeline

findings.title: Findings converge on the definition of "app code under `apps.directory`"
findings.why_it_matters: The design decides three separate times which files under the apps directory count as app code: the precheck's set (D2), the eviction set (D3) and the watcher trigger (D4). The code already has two more answers for the same directory. The startup scan skips `APP_SCAN_EXCLUDE_DIRS` (`.venv`, `venv`, `site-packages`, `.git`, ...), and the watcher uses watchfiles' default filter. Four findings each adjust one of these sets: eviction reaches into a virtualenv (3), the precheck's scope (11), precheck and eviction walking `sys.modules` separately (15), and directory events (16). Does this mean one definition should back every set, rather than four local fixes? That re-evaluation is open-ended. It includes whether some sets should differ on purpose.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate the definition of app code under `apps.directory` before addressing Findings 3, 11, 15 and 16 individually. Open questions: what is the one predicate? Does it reuse `APP_SCAN_EXCLUDE_DIRS`, the watcher's filter, or neither? Does it exclude the running interpreter's environment and hassette's own install? Do directory events count? Is the precheck's "loaded or all" choice a filter over that set?
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate the definition of app code

findings.title: Eviction by `__file__` removes installed packages when the apps directory contains an environment
findings.why_it_matters: D3 evicts every `sys.modules` entry whose `__file__` resolves inside `apps.directory`, whatever its name. Suppose the apps directory holds a virtualenv. The repo's own example sets `directory = "."`, so a user who copies it into a project root with `.venv` beside the app files gets that layout. Reload-all then evicts `hassette`, `pydantic`, `hassette_wire` and everything else installed there. The re-import creates second copies of the core classes, `isinstance` against `App`, `BaseState` and the registries breaks process-wide, and only a process restart recovers. The same layout works today, because the loader imports only configured app files. The startup scan already skips `.venv`, `venv` and `site-packages` in this same directory. D3 doesn't.
findings.recommended: B: Keep matching by file, but skip any module whose path has a part in `APP_SCAN_EXCLUDE_DIRS` or lies under `sys.prefix`, `sys.base_prefix` or hassette's own package directory.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: Eviction runs before the stops, so old instances import new code during shutdown
findings.why_it_matters: The Summary orders the work as precheck, take the locks, evict, then `_restart_apps_unlocked`. That function stops every instance before it starts any. While the old instances stop (`on_shutdown`, in-flight handlers), anything that imports at call time finds the module gone and imports the new file from disk: a function-level `import`, `importlib.import_module`, `typing.get_type_hints`, or Pydantic resolving a forward reference. Old app code then runs against the new helper, and any failure lands in per-app shutdown logging.
findings.recommended: A: Evict after the last stop completes and before the first create, inside `_restart_apps_unlocked`. Update the Summary's orchestration bullet and the Assumed restart bullet.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D8's worst-outcome status adds a second per-item field to `ProblemDetail`
findings.why_it_matters: D8-A adds `ProblemDetail.app_outcomes` beside the existing per-instance `outcomes`. A client then reads per-app detail from a 200 `ReloadAllResponse` on success and from a 500 or 409 problem body otherwise. That's two shapes, and the decision is hard to reverse once the released client parses them. The critic argues that a batch where one of 60 apps fails is a result, not a verdict on one action.
findings.recommended: A: Keep D8 as ratified.
findings.chosen: B: Answer 200 whenever the reload ran
findings.choice_reason: Asked for peer evidence; Elasticsearch _bulk shape changed the recommendation

findings.title: D4's globals scan misses plain-value imports, one of the two hautomate cases it exists for
findings.why_it_matters: D4-B decides that an app module is imported by looking in other modules' globals for the module itself or an object whose `__module__` names it. `vacuum_health.py` does `from hautomate.vacuum_alert import ERROR_STATE, NO_ERROR`, and both are `str` constants with no `__module__`. So an edit to `vacuum_alert` stays a per-app reimport, and `vacuum_health` silently keeps the old values. Only `car_climate`'s `from hautomate.thermoscura import c_to_f`, a function, is caught. The ledger documents only function-level and dynamic imports as misses. The structural-minimalist adds that the scan infers dependencies from leftover state instead of reading them.
findings.recommended: B: Replace the scan with an `ast` read of each loaded apps-dir module's `import` and `from` nodes, resolving relative imports.
findings.chosen: B: Replace the scan with an ast read

findings.title: A separate `reload_all` orchestrator duplicates `apply_changes`, and the Summary and D7 describe the manual path differently
findings.why_it_matters: The Summary adds a `reload_all(...)` method on the mixin, a `reload_all` flag on `ChangeSet` with its own branch in `apply_changes`, and manual triggers that call `AppHandler.reload_all` directly. D7's ratified text says the manual path is `handle_change_event` with `reload_all` forced, under `_change_event_lock`. So the ledger gives two paths for the same thing. `apply_changes` already decides each key under sorted locks, applies `should_auto_reconcile` (D1), builds `AppRestart(force_reload=True)` and calls `_restart_apps_unlocked`. Reload-all is that flow with `reimport_apps` widened to every key, plus a precheck and an eviction.
findings.recommended: A: One entry. The manual trigger and the watcher both feed the existing flow, with `reimport_apps` widened to every key and an evict step. Drop the separate orchestrator and the `ChangeSet.reload_all` flag.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: The per-app outcomes D8 reports have no path back to the manual caller
findings.why_it_matters: D8 puts each app's outcomes in the response. But `_restart_apps_unlocked` logs them ("No response carries these outcomes"), and `apply_changes` and `handle_change_event` both return `None`. Getting the outcomes out means a signature change through three layers plus `AppHandler.reload_all`, and the ledger doesn't list it.
findings.recommended: A: Return the outcomes dict from `_restart_apps_unlocked` and carry it up through `apply_changes` and the entry point to the route.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: A manual reload-all before bootstrap release gets no answer
findings.why_it_matters: Before bootstrap release, `handle_change_event` records a deferred reconciliation and returns. A manual reload-all routed through it (D7) at that moment gets no result and no refusal. The Assumed bullet promises "the same bootstrap-released ... admission rules", and single-app start and reload answer the `bootstrap_not_released` problem in that state.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D6's busy check and the lock acquisition are separated by awaits
findings.why_it_matters: The single-app routes are race-free only because the operation reaches the lock without suspending. Under D7, the path suspends between the route's busy check and the key locks: `refresh_config` awaits `resolve_only_apps` and `persist_manifests`, and the precheck runs before the locks. A single-app action or watcher event that starts in that gap makes a `wait=false` request block behind it, which is the hang D6's default exists to prevent.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D2's precheck can't refuse a brand-new helper with a syntax error, and the stance means every app has already stopped
findings.why_it_matters: D2-B compiles the loaded apps-dir modules plus every enabled app's file. Suppose a deploy adds a new helper with a syntax error and edits apps to import it. That helper isn't checked. The reload stops everything, and the importing apps go `FAILED` with no rollback (A1). The critic proposes compiling every `.py` under the apps directory except hidden and test directories, or, as a stance change, restoring the evicted modules when imports fail. The outage is smaller than the critic's "33 apps" suggests. A widely imported helper is already loaded, so D2-B checks it, and a brand-new file reaches only the apps edited to import it. A top-level runtime error (`NameError`, `ImportError`) in any helper passes every `compile()` precheck, A or B, and fails exactly as a container restart does today.
findings.recommended: A: Keep D2-B as ratified.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: The watcher-triggered reload-all starts manually stopped autostart apps on every helper save
findings.why_it_matters: D1-A restarts every `should_auto_reconcile` key: keys in the registry, plus autostart apps that aren't running. A manually stopped app drops out of the registry, because membership needs an entry holding its `App` and nothing records a manual stop. With the watcher rule on, every helper save therefore starts every stopped autostart app. D1's ratification weighed this for the explicit action. The watcher already does the same narrowly: an edit to a stopped app's own file, or a config change for it, restarts it. Reload-all widens that from "edits to this app" to "edits to any helper".
findings.recommended: A: Keep D1-A for both the manual and the watcher trigger.
findings.chosen: Other: reload-all (both triggers) restarts only keys with a tracked entry (live or FAILED)
findings.choice_reason: Doesn't want reload-all to start manually stopped apps

findings.title: D9's structured `syntax_error` field has no consumer and is hard to remove
findings.why_it_matters: D9 adds a third optional `ProblemDetail` object (`syntax_error` with `file` and `line`) so clients can point at the location. The ratified consumers, the CLI and the UI toast (D11), both show `file:line: msg`, which D9's `detail` already carries. The existing source endpoint is addressed by app key, so it couldn't open a helper file anyway. The field is a wire addition. Adding an optional field later doesn't break the client. Removing one does.
findings.recommended: B: Report the location in `detail` only, and add the structured field when a client needs it.
findings.chosen: B: Report the location in detail only

findings.title: D7 and D9 add two problem codes for one caller outcome, "refused before anything stopped"
findings.why_it_matters: `reload_config_invalid` (D7) and `reload_syntax_error` (D9) are both 409s that mean "nothing ran, and `detail` says why". The critic proposes one `reload_refused` code with the cause in `detail`.
findings.recommended: A: Keep two codes, `reload_config_invalid` and `reload_syntax_error`.
findings.chosen: A: Keep two codes

findings.title: The precheck and the eviction compute "apps-dir modules" separately
findings.why_it_matters: D2-B's precheck set (apps-dir modules in `sys.modules`, plus every enabled app's file) contains D3's eviction set (modules whose `__file__` is under the apps directory). Two helpers that each compute "apps-dir modules" can drift. For example, one picks up Finding 3's exclusions and the other doesn't.
findings.recommended: A: Compute the apps-dir module set in one function that both the precheck and the eviction use.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: A pull that only adds or removes a helper directory doesn't trigger reload-all
findings.why_it_matters: `collapse_changed_paths` skips any path whose parent directory is already in the set, and watchfiles hands it an unordered set. So when a pull creates or deletes a helper directory, the event can carry only the directory, and D4's ".py that isn't an app's own file" test sees nothing. The miss rarely matters in practice. A new helper directory is imported only by app files edited in the same pull, and those are reported and reimported fresh. A deleted directory leaves the old modules loaded until the next reload-all.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a pull that only adds or removes a helper directory doesn't trigger reload-all until the next relevant edit.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 2

findings.title: A `wait=true` request holds `_change_event_lock` and the keys already taken while it waits
findings.why_it_matters: Under D7, a `wait=true` request holds `_change_event_lock` for its whole wait, so watcher events queue behind it. Keys are taken in sorted order, so while it waits on a later busy key, the keys it already holds make single-app actions on those apps answer 409. D6's ratification accepted the unbounded wait, but not these side effects.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: while a `wait=true` request waits, watcher events queue and single-app actions on keys it already holds answer 409.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: while a `wait=true` request waits, watcher events queue and single-app actions on keys it already holds answer 409.

findings.title: Module-scope side effects in helpers run again on every reload-all
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: a helper author who puts side effects at module scope (a long-lived dev loop with the watcher rule on). Evicting and re-importing reruns every helper's top level. A module-scope logging handler, thread, `aiohttp` session, `atexit` hook or connection pool is duplicated on every reload-all, and the old generation's copies are never released. A user `BaseState` subclass registers its converter on import, and a class whose module is removed stays registered.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: module-scope side effects in apps-dir modules run again on each reload-all, and the old generation's resources aren't released.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: module-scope side effects in apps-dir modules run again on each reload-all, and the old generation's resources aren't released.

findings.title: The reload-all log doesn't record what was evicted or how long each phase took
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: an unattended deploy (script or watcher) with nobody watching the response. The Posture logs one INFO summary line (trigger, app count, outcome counts) plus the existing per-app lines. On the watcher path, the log is the only record. The summary omits the evicted module count, the precheck result and the durations of the stop and start phases. Each per-app failure line already includes a short traceback, so the helper behind a FAILED app is usually named.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: the reload-all log has one summary line plus the per-app lines, with no eviction list or phase timings.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: the reload-all log has one summary line plus the per-app lines, with no eviction list or phase timings.

findings.title: D10's `reload --all` carries mutual-exclusion rules a separate command wouldn't
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: a CLI with no second consumer yet. `app reload [key] [instance] --all` makes the key optional, then needs three usage errors: a key with `--all`, an instance with `--all`, and neither given. `hassette app reload-all [--wait] [--yes]` needs none, mirrors HA's separate `reload_all` service, and sits next to `reload` in `app --help`.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: `reload --all` makes the key optional and enforces three usage errors.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: `reload --all` makes the key optional and enforces three usage errors.

findings.title: Editor lock files, `.git`, `.venv` and other noise restart every app under D4
Findings converge on D12's steps before the locks: a config refresh that commits, steered by inputs that aren't known yet
findings.why_it_matters: D12's steps 0-4 decide everything that can still refuse a reload-all: lock-busy, admission, config validity, the syntax precheck and the key-lock busy test. Two critics hit that stretch from different sides. Step 2 calls `refresh_config`, which already swaps `hassette.config`, overwrites the registry's manifests and writes them to the DB before steps 3 and 4 can refuse. A refusal there leaves the new config committed and the diff baseline gone (Finding 3). Steps 2 and 3 branch on `reload_all`, but for a watcher event that value only exists after `detect_changes` has run against the refreshed config, which happens in step 4 (Finding 2). And `reload_all` arrives as one of three boolean inputs (`reload_all`, `manual`, `wait`) that every step branches on (Finding 4). Each finding proposes its own local patch: reorder the steps, record a baseline on refusal, or replace the flags with a policy value. Together they suggest the pre-lock stretch is the problem. Should D12 be re-evaluated as a whole: what the entry point takes as input, what it may change before the last refusal has passed, and where `reload_all` is derived? The re-evaluation is open-ended. It includes accepting some of these behaviours and documenting them.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate D12's steps 0-4 before addressing Findings 2, 3 and 4 individually. Open questions: may anything (`hassette.config`, registry manifests, the DB) change before the last refusal has passed? What is the entry point's input, and where is `reload_all` derived for a watcher event? Against which config does the watcher classify a changed path? If something must be committed before a refusal, what keeps the baseline? Is "manual vs watcher" one policy or several flags?
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate D12's steps 0-4

findings.title: For a watcher event, `reload_all` is needed by D12 steps 2 and 3 but only exists after step 4's detection
findings.why_it_matters: `reconcile_from_disk` takes `reload_all` as a parameter. For the watcher, the Summary says the value comes "from D4's rule via `ChangeSet.reload_all`". But `ChangeSet` comes out of `detect_changes(original, current, ...)`, which needs the refreshed config. D4's "an app's own file" test is `app.full_path in changed`, checked against current manifests. Step 2 (refuse on an invalid config "when `reload_all` is set") and step 3 (precheck "only when `reload_all` is set") both run before step 4 builds anything. So the order can't be implemented for the watcher as written. Classifying against the pre-refresh manifests instead would count a newly added app's file as "not an app file" and trigger a reload-all whenever a pull adds an app. A watcher event with an invalid toml plus a helper change has no defined behaviour: refuse (if `reload_all` were known) or keep the old config (if not). The flag is also both an output of the entry point and one of its inputs.
findings.recommended: A: The entry point takes the trigger (manual, or watcher with paths). Inside, the config is read without raising, detection and D4's classification run, and only then is `reload_all` known. The invalid-config refusal (when `reload_all`) and the precheck then run before step 4's locks.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: A refusal after the config refresh leaves the new config committed and the diff baseline gone
findings.why_it_matters: D12 refreshes the config at step 2 and can then refuse at step 3 (syntax error) or step 4 (a busy key under `wait=false`). By then `refresh_config` has swapped `hassette.config`, replaced the registry's manifests and upserted them to the DB. The next reconcile reads its baseline from `registry.manifests`, which is already the new config, so the old-against-new diff is empty. The config change is then never applied: new autostart apps never start, removed apps keep running, enable/disable and autostart flips are lost, and per-instance `app_config` edits restart only if the key happens to be in the tracked set. The toml and the DB say "new", the running apps are "old", and nothing remembers the gap. Today's watcher can't hit this, because nothing refuses between the refresh and the apply. The refusals this design adds create it. An invalid toml is the exception: `config.reload()` swaps nothing when validation fails.
findings.recommended: B: Run the config build, the precheck and the busy test before mutating `hassette.config`, the registry or the DB, and commit the candidate only once every lock is held. Same test.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: `manual` and `wait` are mode flags that steer five behaviours, alongside `reload_all`
findings.why_it_matters: `reconcile_from_disk(changed_paths, *, reload_all, manual, wait)` takes three booleans. `manual` selects raise-or-defer before release (step 1), raise-or-log on an invalid config (step 2) and on a syntax error (step 3), fail-fast-or-wait (steps 0 and 4), and whether outcomes are returned. `wait` means something only when `manual` is true, and the watcher always passes `wait=True`. `reload_all` is a free choice only for the watcher. That is eight combinations, of which three are valid. D12's "one path" is two behaviours selected by flags inside every step. A third trigger (a scheduled reload, a manual per-app config refresh) has to pick a combination nobody listed.
findings.recommended: A: Replace `manual` and `wait` with one caller-policy value carrying refusal delivery (raise or log) and busy handling (fail fast or wait), and derive `reload_all` (Finding 2).
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D12 step 4's restart set bypasses the detector's filters: orphans, disabled and `--app`-blocked keys get restarted or double-stopped
findings.why_it_matters: When `reload_all` is set, D12 step 4 builds the restart set from D1's set (every key with an instance entry) plus the diff's reimport and reload keys. D1's set bypasses `detect_changes`, which is what keeps the buckets disjoint and drops keys that are disabled, removed, or excluded by `--app`. Three things follow. An app that is running and then removed, disabled or excluded in the same reload is both an orphan and a restart. If the lock pass takes it twice, the non-reentrant `AppKeyLock` deadlocks while `_change_event_lock` is held. Otherwise the app is stopped as an orphan and then restarted. A disabled app still has a manifest in the registry (`refresh_config` keeps every manifest regardless of `enabled`), and `_start_app_unlocked` never checks `enabled`, so the restart starts an app the config just turned off. A blocked key with a leftover live or FAILED entry is stopped and then refused by `_start_app_unlocked`'s `AppBlockedError`, which is logged as "should not be reachable". The Assumed bullet's claim that "an `--app`-blocked key isn't restarted" cites `detect_changes`, which this set doesn't go through. D1 reads "no entry" as "someone stopped it". That inference is accepted, but it says nothing about a blocked key that does have an entry, and `registry.is_blocked` is the authority for that.
findings.chosen: In D12 step 4, after "**Restarts:** the D1 set ... together with the config diff's reimport and reload keys", add: "then keep only keys that are enabled in the refreshed config, aren't `registry.is_blocked`, and aren't orphans. Restarts, orphans and new apps are disjoint, so the lock pass takes each key once." Replace the Assumed bullet's "An `--app`-blocked key isn't restarted" evidence (`app_change_detector.py` `only_apps` filtering) with this filter (`app_registry.py` `is_blocked`, D12 step 4). Add a test to D12's build: a running app that the refreshed config removes, disables or blocks is stopped once and never restarted. D1's set (E) is unchanged.

findings.title: "The apps directory" is one `apps.directory`, but each app can carry its own `app_dir`, and the watcher watches those too
findings.why_it_matters: `is_app_code(path, app_dir)`, `app_code_modules`, `evict_apps_package` and the precheck each take one directory, and D3's Ratified sentence says "inside `apps.directory`". But `AppManifest.app_dir` is a required per-app field, the config docs show `[hassette.apps.my_app] app_dir = "src/my_app"`, and the watcher already watches `apps.directory` plus every manifest's `app_dir`. All of those roots load into one synthesized package, because `_ensure_namespace_package` appends each root to the same `__path__`. An app outside `apps.directory`, and its helpers, are never evicted or prechecked (D2 adds only the app's own file), and `is_app_code` rejects their changes, so D4's watcher rule never fires for them. Those apps keep the old helper generation after a reload-all that reports success. The Summary's central claim is that every app ends up on one generation. The "Out of scope" bullet "Reloading modules outside the apps directory" reads as covering site-packages. Whether it was meant to cover per-app roots isn't stated, and the watcher's behaviour argues against that reading.
findings.recommended: A: Make the predicate take the set of app roots (`apps.directory` plus every manifest's `app_dir`) and have the precheck, eviction and D4 all use that one set, keeping D3's per-root exclusions.
findings.chosen: A: Make the predicate take the set of app roots

findings.title: D12 leaves the "nothing to do" gate and the load-completed broadcast unspecified for `reload_all`
findings.why_it_matters: A helper-only edit produces a `ChangeSet` with every bucket empty. `handle_change_event` returns at `if not changes.has_any_change` ("changed but no app changes detected") before anything runs, and `_reconcile_changes` gates `apply_changes` on `has_changes`. Unless that gate counts `reload_all`, the watcher drops the event, which is the drop D4 cites as the problem. D12 never says so. D12 also doesn't say whether the manual path sends `HASSETTE_EVENT_APP_LOAD_COMPLETED`, which `_reconcile_changes` sends so connected dashboards refetch. The critic's third point, that the pre-release replay path would skip reload-all, doesn't hold: no app module is imported before bootstrap release (`start_app` admits before it imports), so the first imports already read the edited files.
findings.chosen: Add to D12, after "A watcher event without `reload_all` runs the same steps...": "Wherever `reload_all` is carried, the 'no app changes detected' gate (`app_lifecycle_changes.py:342`) and the `has_changes` gate in `_reconcile_changes` count it, so a helper-only edit isn't dropped. Both triggers send `HASSETTE_EVENT_APP_LOAD_COMPLETED` after a reload-all runs. The pre-release replay needs no reload-all: no app module is imported before release, so the first imports read the edited files."

findings.title: The new module-graph helpers push `app_utils.py` past the file-size gate
findings.why_it_matters: The Summary puts `is_app_code`, `app_code_modules`, `evict_apps_package`, `precheck_apps_package` and an `ast` import reader in `src/hassette/utils/app_utils.py`, which is 780 lines today. The 800-line HSL102 threshold is close, and the `file-sizes` gate fails a PR that grows a file past it ("a red `file-sizes` check always means this PR regressed something; fix it in-PR", CLAUDE.md). Spec 161 D1 ("`app_utils.py` is the only code that removes app modules") justifies where eviction goes. It doesn't cover the predicate, the precheck or the import reader. The import reader also serves only the watcher classifier in `app_change_detector.py`, so the module-graph code ends up split by caller. The other side: one file keeps everything about app modules together, and a split adds a module to learn.
findings.recommended: A: Put `is_app_code`, `app_code_modules`, `precheck_apps_package` and the `ast` import reader in a new `src/hassette/utils/app_modules.py`, and keep only `evict_apps_package` in `app_utils.py`. Update the Summary's "Where each piece lives".
findings.chosen: A: Put is_app_code, app_code_modules, precheck_apps_package and the ast import reader in a new src/hassette/utils/app_modules.py

findings.title: D12's "no old instance imports new code" ignores stops that walk away, and eviction doesn't look at stop outcomes
findings.why_it_matters: D12's table says old instances lazily importing during shutdown is "not possible: eviction follows the last stop". A stop can end as a walk-away, with pending tasks or a raised shutdown: the instance is FAILED, flagged needs-restart, and its tasks may still be running. That work is old-generation code, and after step 6 any import it makes at call time finds the new file. The flagged instance stays until a process restart, so the mixed generation persists in it. Because it is already flagged and refused on later actions, the cost is a confusing traceback in an instance already marked as needing a restart, not corrupted state.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: an instance whose stop walked away can keep running old-generation work that imports new modules until the process restarts; it is already flagged needs-restart.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: an instance whose stop walked away can keep running old-generation work that imports new modules until the process restarts; it is already flagged needs-restart.

findings.title: Eviction never calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()`, so a newly created helper can be missed
findings.why_it_matters: `evict_apps_package` removes `sys.modules` entries, `APP_MODULES` records, parent attributes and cached bytecode, but nothing in `src/` calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()`. The path finder caches each directory's listing and refreshes it only when the directory's mtime changes. If a pull adds a helper file and a reload-all imports it within the filesystem's mtime granularity of the last cached listing, the import can miss the file, and the importing app goes FAILED with `ModuleNotFoundError` for a file that exists. The Python docs name this case for modules created after the interpreter started. App files themselves load by path, so this only affects helpers.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: on a filesystem with coarse directory mtimes, a helper created within one mtime tick of the last import from its directory can be missed, and its importers go FAILED until the next reload-all.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: on a filesystem with coarse directory mtimes, a helper created within one mtime tick of the last import from its directory can be missed, and its importers go FAILED until the next reload-all.

findings.title: D3 doesn't say what eviction does with namespace sub-packages that have no `__file__`
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: apps with nested helper directories, as hautomate has. `app_code_modules` selects by `__file__`. A helper directory with no `__init__.py` is a namespace package whose `__file__` is `None`, so it is never evicted. D3 says the top-level synthesized package is kept but is silent on sub-packages. The parent-attribute deletion removes the evicted submodules' attributes, so what stays is an empty package object. If a pull deletes the directory, that object stays in `sys.modules` with a dead `__path__` until restart. It's harmless unless something imports from it.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: namespace sub-packages with no `__file__` are kept, so a deleted helper directory leaves an empty package object in `sys.modules` until restart.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: namespace sub-packages with no `__file__` are kept, so a deleted helper directory leaves an empty package object in `sys.modules` until restart.
